- Overestimate bullish sentiment spikes: When sentiment rises sharply (e.g., >0.80), model tends to overreact with excessive upward bias; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% relative to sentiment peak.
- Underestimate bearish sentiment dips: When sentiment falls below 0.20, model often undercorrects or ignores the dip; adjust downward by 3–7% to reflect sentiment-driven mean reversion.
- Lagged overreaction: Model frequently overshoots after recent highs/lows, especially in 30-day horizon; apply a 1–2 day lag correction to smooth out momentum-driven peaks.
- Mean reversion bias: Model tends to overpredict continuation of recent trends; apply a 1–3% downward adjustment if recent 5-day average is above 78.5.
- Horizon mismatch: 30-day forecasts often overestimate volatility in early periods; reduce forecast variance by 10–15% if sentiment is stable or low.
- Sentiment-weighted adjustment: If sentiment >0.60, reduce forecast by 2–5% for each 0.10 above 0.60; if sentiment <0.40, increase forecast by 2–5% for each 0.10 below 0.40.
